Express the probability of not being late along each branch: by bus it is $1 - 0.4 = 0.6$, and by bicycle it is $1 - x$.

walkthrough:
Identify the probabilities of not being late for each travel method:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Bus}) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$$
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Cycle}) = 1 - x$$

Use the Law of Total Probability to set up an equation for overall probability of not being late:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late}) = \mathrm{P}(\text{Bus}) \times \mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Bus}) + \mathrm{P}(\text{Cycle}) \times \mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Cycle}) = 0.63$$
$$0.8(0.6) + 0.2(1 - x) = 0.63$$

ai_rubric.Solving Unknown Probabilities: Sets up total probability equation 0.8*0.6 + 0.2*(1 - x) = 0.63 and solves for x = 0.25.

teacher_walkthrough: Shona travels to college either by bus (probability $0.8$) or by bicycle (probability $0.2$). We are given the overall probability that she is not late on a random day is $0.63$.

Step 1: Determine the conditional probabilities of being on time (not late):
- If she takes the bus, the probability she is late is $0.4$, so the probability she is not late is:
  $$1 - 0.4 = 0.6$$
- If she cycles, the probability she is late is $x$, so the probability she is not late is:
  $$1 - x$$

Step 2: Apply the Law of Total Probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Not Late}) = \mathrm{P}(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late}) + \mathrm{P}(\text{Cycle} \cap \text{Not Late})$$
$$0.8 \times 0.6 + 0.2 \times (1 - x) = 0.63$$

Step 3: Expand and simplify the linear equation:
$$0.48 + 0.20 - 0.20x = 0.63$$
$$0.68 - 0.20x = 0.63$$
Subtract $0.68$ from both sides:
$$-0.20x = 0.63 - 0.68 = -0.05$$
Divide by $-0.20$:
$$x = \frac{-0.05}{-0.20} = 0.25$$
